category: torrent-side aggregator (Stremio addon over multiple public trackers, debrid-aware)

free_tier.stated: Anonymous: GET /stream/movie/tt1254207.json returned 5,709 bytes of JSON with infoHash, fileIdx and per-stream size and seeders, with no key and no account.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: the addon returns magnet hashes, not bytes

retention.stated: not applicable: results are computed per request; the debrid cache behind them is the provider's retention

egress.terms: No byte allowance from the addon: it returns magnet links, and the transfer is between a user (or the debrid provider) and the swarm.

interface_detail: Stremio addon protocol over HTTP: /stream/<type>/<imdb>.json, /manifest.json and a /configure page that takes a debrid key. Every response is JSON.
tooling: Any HTTP client. Stremio or a Kodi addon consumes it directly; AIOStreams, MediaFusion and StremThru chain it behind a single addon. The debrid path needs the provider's API key in the config URL.
chaining: Torrentio resolves an IMDb id to magnets from public trackers, and with a debrid key it asks the provider which hashes are cached; that cached answer is what makes playback start without seeding.

limits.value: no published limit on torrentio.strem.fun; the only published statement is from the operator of a shared public instance, who reports that its traffic to Torrentio was rate-limited
not published; the add-on is a shared host, so the limit is its capacity rather than a documented number

limits_note: The addon returns a per-title stream list; each title opened is one request. Its own cache headers are explicit: cacheMaxAge 3600, staleRevalidate 14400, staleError 604800, so one title is cheap to ask twice and a shared proxy is what multiplies the rate. Torrentio has also been down for hosting reasons more than once (issues 288 and 370).
binding_note: There is no byte accounting anywhere in the addon; the only thing that breaks at scale is the request rate from one address, which is exactly what the shared-instance reports describe.

identity_cost.detail: No account for the P2P path. A debrid key is optional and is the provider's, not Torrentio's.

reliability_note: Hosting moves and blocks: the tracker's own issues record the VPS being blocked (issue 288) and a DDoS (issue 370), each taking the public instance down for days. The addon's cacheMaxAge is 3600 s, so a cached stream list can outlive the swarm it describes.
confidence_note: One stream request was executed on 2026-10-23 and returned real magnets. The rate figure stays reported, because the number came from a third-party operator rather than from Torrentio.

evidence.proved: HTTP 200 JSON, 5,709 bytes, streams carrying name 'Torrentio', infoHash f181e166e440b355ce73cc8b988f47ad7e8ea6ab, '7.1 GB' and seed counts, with no key supplied
a maintainer states the shared public instance 'probably got rate limited by Torrentio' because all its users' requests come from one address
the addon maintainer wrote that torrentio's VPS was blocked and the addon would be down until a new host was found; read from the issue title and quoted reply in search results, not opened

version v0.0.15, the scraped provider list, and 'RealDebrid/Premiumize/AllDebrid/DebridLink/EasyDebrid/Offcloud/TorBox/Put.io support' on the configuration page - which came back with upstream_status 403 and full body text

notes: Caution: the addon is not an index you can crawl by title, it is a per-title resolver, so 1 TiB/month means thousands of per-title requests and the request rate is the whole story. Listed because the client layer is what makes a free key usable at all, and because it names two providers outside the eight (EasyDebrid, Offcloud) that the next breadth pass should pick up.
